purpose: Prospectively confirm whether the Train-160-selected PPARG MD receptor pair improves early enrichment over its frozen best single receptor on the untouched Stage19a fresh-validation panel.

train_selection.per_receptor_normalization: Empirical midrank CDF fitted on all 160 Stage32 training rows; lower fractions are favorable.
train_selection.set_aggregation: minimum normalized rank fraction across selected receptors
train_selection.primary: median score across seed0, seed1, and seed2
train_selection.sensitivity: minimum score across seed0, seed1, and seed2
train_selection.robust_utility: (primary BEDROC20 + mean seed BEDROC20 + worst seed BEDROC20)/3
train_selection.single_rule: Enumerate all 16 singletons and choose maximum robust utility, breaking ties by receptor ID.
train_selection.pair_rule: Enumerate all 120 pairs and choose maximum robust utility, breaking ties by sorted receptor IDs.
train_selection.validation_comparator: The frozen best singleton, whether or not it is a member of the selected pair.

ligand_preparation.macrocycle_policy: Run Meeko flexible first; rerun with rigid macrocycles after failure or closure-pseudoatom detection; require zero remaining closure pseudoatoms.

confirmation_analysis.normalization: Transform fresh-validation scores with the receptor- and scenario-specific empirical CDF frozen from all 160 training rows.
confirmation_analysis.pair_aggregation: minimum normalized fraction across the two selected receptors
confirmation_analysis.primary_metric: BEDROC with alpha=20 on median-seed scores
confirmation_analysis.paired_uncertainty: 2000 label-stratified ligand bootstrap replicates with seed stage32b-pparg-md-pair-bootstrap-v1

decision_boundary: A pass confirms only that the frozen PPARG MD pair prospectively improves fresh-validation early enrichment over its frozen single-receptor comparator. It does not revive the failed Stage32a QUBO-efficacy gate, access the locked test set, demonstrate cross-target transfer, quantum execution, speedup, or quantum advantage.
